brief.conference_theme: Environmental and social regeneration: beyond sustainability
brief.panel_theme: Circularity at scale: regenerative sourcing and supply chains

plan.summary: Build a three-person panel on circularity at scale, focusing on regenerative sourcing and supply chains in business. Favor rising or established, budget-conscious candidates with prior conference or presentation experience, and balance sectors, career stages, places, and organization types; national reach allows searches beyond New Haven.
plan.location_focus: National; include New Haven and the Northeast where useful

angles: Business-school and supply-chain researchers studying circular procurement, regenerative agriculture, and scaling reuse
Researchers presenting at circular economy and sustainable business conferences
Corporate sourcing, procurement, and supply-chain leaders implementing circular or regenerative practices
Circular-economy consultants and nonprofit program leaders with practical case studies and conference presentations
State or federal circular-economy, sustainable materials, and responsible-sourcing policy specialists
Think-tank policy experts on producer responsibility and circular supply chains who present to business audiences
Founders of early-stage circular materials, reuse, and regenerative sourcing businesses with demonstrated scale-up work
Small and mid-sized company leaders presenting supply-chain circularity case studies at industry events
Nonprofit and coalition leaders advancing just, regenerative supply chains and circular sourcing
Community or worker-centered advocates connecting materials circularity with equitable sourcing, with public speaking experience
Business or sustainability reporters covering circular supply chains, regenerative sourcing, and materials innovation
Trade-publication editors or podcast hosts who moderate circular economy and sustainable business discussions

cards.name: Aditya Vedantam
cards.job_title: Associate Professor, Operations Management and Strategy; Affiliated Faculty, Center for Supply Chain Analytics
cards.organization: University at Buffalo School of Management
cards.could_speak_on: What operations research and business-model design can teach companies about making circular supply chains work at scale.
talk_ideas: Sustainable operations and circular business models
Trade-in and resale models: balancing profitability and environmental footprint
Remanufacturing contracts and supply-chain quality uncertainty
cards.bio: Aditya Vedantam is an Associate Professor of Operations Management and Strategy at the University at Buffalo School of Management and affiliated faculty at its Center for Supply Chain Analytics. His research interests include sustainable operations management, supply-chain management, and new business models for a circular economy.
credentials: PhD, Krannert School of Management, Purdue University
cards.why_fit: His business-school research connects circular business models, operations, and supply-chain analytics—the practical scaling questions at the center of this panel.

past_speaking.event: Talks based on his research to the Institute of Supply Management
Talks based on his research to the Western New York Sustainable Business Roundtable
Talks based on his research to the Association of Plastic Recyclers

notable_work: Research on trade-in versus selling in peer-to-peer marketplaces and environmental footprint
Research on revenue-sharing contracts under quality uncertainty in remanufacturing
cards.fit_reason: His research directly addresses sustainable operations and circular business models, and the faculty page confirms multiple industry and professional-audience talks.

cards.name: Joseph Sarkis
cards.could_speak_on: How circular-economy principles and sustainable supply-chain practices can move from research into large-scale business operations.
talk_ideas: Scaling circular supply chains across industries
Environmental sustainability in supply-chain management
Circular economy approaches to sustainable sourcing
cards.bio: Joseph Sarkis is a Professor of Management in Worcester Polytechnic Institute’s Business School, with an affiliated role in Management Engineering. His education includes a PhD in Management Sciences from SUNY at Buffalo, and his work includes sustainable supply chains and the circular economy.
credentials: PhD, Management Sciences, SUNY at Buffalo
cards.why_fit: His research and academic role provide a systems-level business perspective on scaling circularity and sustainability across supply chains.
notable_work: Two-volume reference work on supply chain management, published by Palgrave Macmillan
cards.fit_reason: Directly relevant academic expertise in circular economy and sustainable supply chains, with a confirmed public podcast appearance.

cards.name: Christopher Marquis
cards.organization: Cambridge Judge Business School, University of Cambridge
cards.could_speak_on: How regenerative agriculture and corporate accountability can reshape the environmental and social impacts embedded in supply chains.
talk_ideas: Regenerative agriculture and the roots of value chains
Corporate accountability for supply-chain environmental and social impacts
Business sustainability and the transition beyond conventional sustainability
cards.bio: Christopher Marquis is the Sinyi Professor of Chinese Management at Cambridge Judge Business School and a Fellow and Director of Studies at Jesus College. His research examines business sustainability, social entrepreneurship, and historical processes; he is the author of The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs.
credentials: Author of The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs
cards.why_fit: His work on business sustainability and regenerative agriculture offers a strong connection to the panel’s regenerative-sourcing theme and a business accountability perspective.

past_speaking.event: Climate Rising podcast: “Regenerative Agriculture and ‘The Profiteers’”

notable_work: The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs
Better Business: How the B Corp Movement is Remaking Capitalism

links.label: Climate Rising podcast episode on regenerative agriculture

cards.fit_reason: Strong fit for regenerative sourcing and corporate accountability, with a confirmed public podcast appearance; his profile is less specifically focused on supply-chain operations.

dropped.name: Nazli Turken
dropped.reason: The provided faculty profile blocked access, and no other source was available in this verification pass to confirm her current academic role.

cards.name: Deborah Dull
cards.organization: Circular Supply Chain Network; Trillium Digital Services
cards.could_speak_on: How companies can operationalize circular supply chains, scale material recovery, and use supply-chain strategy to support regenerative sourcing.
talk_ideas: Circular supply chains: practical steps from sourcing through recovery
Scaling circularity across global supply networks
Using data and supply-chain orchestration to reduce risk and improve resource flows
cards.bio: Deborah Dull founded the Circular Supply Chain Network and is Managing Partner of Trillium Digital Services. Her work and speaking focus on supply-chain strategy and circularity, informed by experience at Microsoft, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, GE, and other organizations.
credentials: BA in Supply Chain & Operations Management, Western Washington University
cards.why_fit: She brings an operational supply-chain perspective directly aligned with the panel's focus on scaling circularity and regenerative sourcing, and has documented experience speaking on these topics.
cards.fit_reason: Strong match on practical circular supply-chain operations, with multiple documented talks and relevant organizational leadership.

cards.name: Monica Becker
cards.organization: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
cards.could_speak_on: How cross-industry collaborations and product standards can embed circularity and safer materials into supply chains at scale.
talk_ideas: Building industry collaborations for circular product and material systems
Using product standards to support circular sourcing and design
From safer chemistry initiatives to value-chain implementation
cards.bio: Monica Becker is Senior Director of Strategy & Development at the Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute, where she leads growth, innovation, and impact initiatives across sectors. Her prior work includes cross-industry sustainability collaborations, product-sector programs, and sustainability consulting.
credentials: Master’s degrees in Civil & Environmental Engineering and Technology & Policy, MIT
B.S. in Engineering, College of Environmental Science and Forestry
cards.why_fit: She offers a practitioner’s view of turning circular-economy and safer-material goals into collaborative initiatives across product value chains.

past_speaking.event: Clean and Ingestible Beauty Virtual Event panels
GC3 Annual Innovators Roundtable workshops and panels

links.label: Clean and Ingestible Beauty speaker page

cards.fit_reason: Strong cross-sector implementation experience, with documented panels and leadership focused on circularity and sustainable product value chains.

cards.name: Heidi Sanborn
cards.could_speak_on: How producer-responsibility policy and practical implementation can help businesses redesign products and scale circular supply chains.
talk_ideas: Making extended producer responsibility work for circular supply chains
Designing products for recyclability and lower waste
Connecting industry, government, and the public to implement circular-economy policy
cards.bio: Heidi Sanborn is identified with the National Stewardship Action Council and is described as a solid-waste industry leader with 35 years of experience. Her work has involved industry, government, and the public on waste reduction, product design, recyclability, and environmental policy.
credentials: 35 years of experience in the solid-waste industry, according to the Circular Indiana conference page
cards.why_fit: She offers a policy-and-implementation perspective relevant to business decisions about product design, producer responsibility, and circular material flows.

past_speaking.event: 2026 Circular Indiana Conference keynote and Policy & Practice panel

notable_work: Work with industry, government, and the public on waste reduction, product design, recyclability, and policy implementation

links.label: Circular Indiana 2026 speaker and program page

cards.fit_reason: The source confirms her extensive circular-economy policy and implementation experience and a 2026 keynote and panel appearance.

cards.name: Anthony Levy
cards.could_speak_on: How circular IT reuse and life-extension strategies can make supply chains more resource-efficient while creating business value.
talk_ideas: Scaling reuse and remanufacturing in technology supply chains
Measuring embodied carbon and Scope 3 impacts of IT equipment
Building commercial models for extending the life of critical infrastructure
cards.bio: Anthony Levy is Founder and CEO of Circularity First, a group of sustainable IT companies. His work focuses on reuse and life extension for technology, and he has advised organizations on integrating sustainability into IT strategies.
credentials: Founder and CEO of Circularity First
MBA in Entrepreneurship, University of California, Los Angeles
cards.why_fit: Offers a practitioner-founder perspective on circular supply chains through technology reuse, reverse logistics, and extending product life; his public profile and summit listing document multiple speaking appearances.

past_speaking.event: UN Global Compact Network UK 2025 Annual Summit, “Transformative Innovation: How ESG Fuels Competitive Advantage”
Sustainability webinar featured on Anthony Levy's site

notable_work: Circularity First reuse and repurposing of technology to reduce e-waste and embodied carbon

links.label: UN Global Compact Network UK speaker profile

cards.fit_reason: Strong direct match: founder-led circular IT reuse with documented business outcomes and more than one public speaking appearance.

cards.name: Naomi Davis
cards.could_speak_on: How community-rooted green economies and neighborhood resource systems can make circularity work for residents as well as supply chains.
talk_ideas: Building local circular economies through neighborhood-scale resource systems
Connecting waste, horticulture, housing, and energy to community wealth
Designing circular initiatives around community resilience and self-reliance
cards.bio: Naomi Davis is the founder and CEO of Blacks in Green, a nonprofit focused on environmental economic development and transforming Black communities through the green economy. Its Sustainable Square Mile approach emphasizes community resilience and local systems.
cards.why_fit: Offers a community-led nonprofit perspective that can ground a business-focused conversation about regenerative supply chains in neighborhood needs and economic benefits.
cards.fit_reason: Directly connects circularity with community-centered economic development and has a confirmed Circularity 24 speaking appearance.

cards.name: Catherine Weetman
cards.could_speak_on: How businesses can put circular and regenerative strategies into practice across sourcing, products, and supply chains.
talk_ideas: Circular business models that build resilience and value across supply chains
Practical approaches to regenerative strategies in food and fashion
Lessons from supply-chain roles at Tesco, Kellogg’s, and DHL Supply Chain
cards.bio: Catherine Weetman is an author, speaker, and podcaster focused on circular and regenerative business strategies. Her experience spans manufacturing, food, fashion, consulting, and senior roles at Tesco, Kellogg’s, and DHL Supply Chain; she hosts the Circular Economy Podcast.
credentials: Fellow of the Institute for Sustainability and Environmental Professionals (ISEP) and member of its Circular Economy Steering Group
Author of A Circular Economy Handbook
cards.why_fit: Offers a direct business and supply-chain perspective on circularity, with documented experience speaking to business audiences and running talks and workshops.

past_speaking.event: United Nations College Circular Economy and the 2030 Agenda course webinars

notable_work: A Circular Economy Handbook: How to Build a More Resilient, Competitive and Sustainable Business
cards.fit_reason: Strongest direct match: circular-economy expertise, supply-chain experience, regenerative business focus, and verified speaking work.

cards.name: Nina Pullman
cards.could_speak_on: What reporting from food and agricultural supply chains reveals about sourcing impacts and the practical challenges of more sustainable food systems.
talk_ideas: Tracing the environmental impacts behind food supply chains
What producers and communities experience in commodity supply chains
How food journalism can connect sourcing choices to sustainability outcomes
cards.bio: Nina Pullman is a freelance journalist, producer, and editor specializing in food, supply chains, farming, sustainability, environment, and travel. She has made programmes and podcasts for BBC Radio 4 and BBC World Service, founded and edited Wicked Leeks, and reported on agricultural supply chains in South and Central America.
cards.why_fit: Brings an editorial and food-sourcing perspective, including reporting on avocado, banana, and coffee production and experience producing and presenting radio.
notable_work: Founded and edited Wicked Leeks, a magazine for sustainable food and ethical business
Who Gives a Fork podcast on stories in popular food supply chains
cards.fit_reason: A strong food-supply-chain communicator with field reporting and broadcast experience; offers a distinct editorial perspective.

cards.name: Heather Clancy
cards.could_speak_on: How corporate climate innovation and business-model change intersect with efforts to scale circular and regenerative supply chains.
talk_ideas: Corporate business-model innovation for a low-carbon economy
The role of technology in business climate action
What business-climate reporting reveals about scaling environmental solutions
cards.bio: Heather Clancy is an award-winning journalist specializing in transformative technology and climate tech. As editor at large for Trellis.net, formerly GreenBiz, she covers how corporations use business-model innovation and technology to support a low-carbon economy. Her journalism has appeared in Entrepreneur, Fortune, The International Herald Tribune, and The New York Times.
credentials: Co-author of Niche Down: How to Become Legendary By Being Different
cards.why_fit: A business-climate journalist who can help a business audience examine the corporate innovation and technology dimensions of scaling circularity.
notable_work: Co-authored Niche Down: How to Become Legendary By Being Different
cards.fit_reason: Strong business-climate communications background, but the reviewed page did not establish prior public speaking or a direct supply-chain specialization.
